Introduction to forecasting

What is a forecast?

Estimating how a sequence of observations will continue into the future, using all information available now.

What data do we need?

  1. Historical data on the variable to forecast
  2. Past and future values of predictors
    • Deterministic (e.g. holidays)
    • Stochastic (e.g. temperature)
  3. Expert knowledge and context
    • New information

Why forecast?

Why do you use forecasts?

Decision Forecast
Build a new hospital in the next 10 years? ?
Call centre staff needed next week? ?
Vaccine doses needed next month? ?
  • Supports planning
  • Informs decisions
  • Provides evidence

Your time series

What time series do you work with?

What makes it a time series?

Observations + when they happened.

  • The time column is the index
  • Observations are ordered in time
  • The frequency matters

tsibble objects

A tsibble has three parts

A tsibble stores one or more time series in a table.

  • Index: when
  • Key: which series (optional)
  • Measures: what was observed

Works with tidyverse functions.

The tsibble index

For annual data, integer years work as the index:

mydata <- tsibble(
  year = 2012:2016,
  y = c(123, 39, 78, 52, 110),
  index = year
)
mydata
# A tsibble: 5 x 2 [1Y]
   year     y
  <int> <dbl>
1  2012   123
2  2013    39
3  2014    78
4  2015    52
5  2016   110

The tsibble index

z
# A tibble: 5 × 2
  Month    Observation
  <chr>          <dbl>
1 2019 Jan          50
2 2019 Feb          23
3 2019 Mar          34
4 2019 Apr          30
5 2019 May          25
  • "2019 Jan" is just text
  • More frequent than yearly? Use a time class

The tsibble index

z |>
  mutate(Month = yearmonth(Month)) |>
  as_tsibble(index = Month)
# A tsibble: 5 x 2 [1M]
     Month Observation
     <mth>       <dbl>
1 2019 Jan          50
2 2019 Feb          23
3 2019 Mar          34
4 2019 Apr          30
5 2019 May          25

The tsibble index

Common time index variables can be created with these functions:

Frequency Function
Annual start:end
Quarterly yearquarter()
Monthly yearmonth()
Weekly yearweek()
Daily as_date(), ymd()
Sub-daily as_datetime(), ymd_hms()

Converting dates

Often data is provided as dates, even if it isn’t daily.

d <- as.Date("2026-10-01")
yearquarter(d)
## <yearquarter[1]>
## [1] "2026 Q4"
## # Year starts on: January
yearmonth(d)
## <yearmonth[1]>
## [1] "2026 Oct"
yearweek(d)
## <yearweek[1]>
## [1] "2026 W40"
## # Week starts on: Monday

Looking ahead: mixtime

One family of linear time classes, including year() and datetime():

library(mixtime)
c(year(d), yearquarter(d), yearmonth(d), date(d))
## <mixtime[4]>
## [1] 2026       2026 Q4    2026 Oct   2026-10-01

Any granularity from a chronon (one time step) and linear_time():

x <- datetime("2024-01-01 00:00:00") + minutes(0:3) * 15L
linear_time(x, chronon = cal_gregorian$minute(15L))
## <mixtime[4]>
## [1] 2024-01-01 00:00 2024-01-01 00:15 2024-01-01 00:30 2024-01-01 00:45
  • yearmonth(d) is linear_time(d, chronon = cal_gregorian$month(1L))

Looking ahead: mixtime

More time types, beyond this course:

# Timezones
datetime(as.POSIXct("2026-10-05 22:30", tz = "UTC"), tz = "Africa/Nairobi")
## <mixtime[1]>
## [1] 2026-10-06 01:30:00 EAT
# Other calendars (also cal_isoweek, lunar and solar calendars)
linear_time(d, chronon = cal_sym454$month(1L))
## <mixtime[1]>
## [1] 2026-Oct
# Cyclical time
day_of_week(d)
## <mixtime[1]>
## [1] Thu
# Durations
yearmonth(d) + months(0:2)
## <mixtime[3]>
## [1] 2026 Oct 2026 Nov 2026 Dec

Declare the index and keys

prison <- readr::read_csv("data/prison_population.csv") |>
  mutate(quarter = yearquarter(date)) |>
  select(-date) |>
  as_tsibble(
    index = quarter,
    key = c(state, gender, legal, indigenous)
  )

Example: Australian pharmaceutical sales

Australian Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme

Australian Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme

The PBS is the Australian government drug subsidy scheme.

  • Subsidises many pharmacy drugs
  • Costs nearly 1% of GDP
  • Budget relies on forecasts of drug usage
  • Split by drug type (ATC2 x84), concession (x2) and patient type (x2)

Your turn

Using tourism

  1. Find the quarterly total Trips for each State
  2. Challenge: Which State had the most Trips over the whole period?

Using PBS

  1. Find the total monthly Scripts for ATC2 "H02"

Hints

  • summarise() always keeps the index
  • group_by() the keys you want to keep
  • as_tibble() drops the index, to summarise over time

Recap

  • A tsibble has an index, keys and measures
  • The index needs a time class (yearmonth(), as_date(), …)
  • Use dplyr verbs to wrangle tsibbles
